gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker 140W 4-Port (A2697) it picked fell from 140 W to 120 W after about 30 minutes in techtest.org's test, while the Chinese lab Chongdiantou ran the AOHi Youth 140W at 28 V/5 A for a full hour and techtest.org reports the Anker Prime 160W holding a constant 140 W.
standout_why: I compared against thegadgetmasters, Macworld, thisUSB, thunderboltlaptop, verdictbits and ChargingGearLab. The first four print no measurements; thisUSB says outright "We haven't put these chargers on a test bench". verdictbits (rank 7 in the first chat, not cited) already carries Tom's Hardware's figures for the A2697 (118 W after 30 minutes, 67.2 °C) and the Baseus FH11, and ChargingGearLab has 139.2 W for 30 minutes on Apple's adapter. So the A2697 throttle is partly known. What no result has is any measurement of the three chargers we link (UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W X774, AOHi The Youth 140W, Anker Prime 160W), the second independent A2697 throttle test, or Notebookcheck's MacBook-side figure that makes a throttle matter.
decides: It does not overturn the map's top three, but it weakens ChatGPT's pick and reorders confidence among ours. Two independent tests (techtest.org; Tom's Hardware as reported by verdictbits) show the Anker A2697 dropping to about 118–120 W after roughly 30 minutes. Notebookcheck measured a 16-inch MacBook Pro M5 Pro drawing 145 W at peak and settling at 134 W on the 140 W adapter, so under sustained heavy load a throttled charger leaves the battery to cover the gap. The AOHi Youth has the strongest published evidence among our rows: a one-hour 28 V/5 A load in a 25 °C chamber, 94.59% efficiency at 110 V, and 126.56 W into a MacBook Pro 16. It ran hot (71–78.9 °C surface) and the unit was the China-market version from 2024. The Anker Prime 160W has two tests saying 140 W holds (techtest.org and smartzone.de), with techtest.org warning 160 W may not. The UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W (X774) has only spot readings into a 16-inch MacBook Pro (131.8 W and 134.82 W, ChargerLAB) and no published sustained 140 W test, so the page should say its 140 W is confirmed as a negotiated profile and a spot reading, not as a long-run figure. Baseus EnerFill FH11 (a partner-store product) should stay off the table: 88 W after 30 minutes and 76.4 °C in Tom's test as reported by verdictbits.

findings.label: Sustained 140 W output (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2025-01-20)
findings.value: about 30 minutes at 140 W, then throttled to 120 W (28 V at 4.28 A); the conclusion gives 100–120 W after throttling
findings.source_title: Der Anker Charger 140W 4-Port PD3.1 A2697 im Test: sehr gut, aber mit Schönheitsfehlern
findings.note: Quote: "nur ca. eine halbe Stunde lang 140 W liefern, ehe sich die Leistung auf 120 W herunterdrosselte." 28 V × 4.28 A = 119.8 W. Room temperature and mains voltage are not stated; a German test, so presumably 230 V, but the review does not say. The display showed "Cooling" mode. No °C figure given.

findings.label: Sustained 140 W and efficiency (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2025-11-28)
findings.value: 140 W constant held; 160 W constant can trigger temperature throttling; 94.7% efficiency at 140 W, 89.4% average, 73.3% lowest; idle about 2.0 W with display on, about 0.64 W with it dimmed; 205 g; 65 × 52 × 36 mm
findings.source_title: Das beste Ladegerät der 140 W Klasse, der Anker Prime Charger 160W im Test
findings.note: Quote: "160 W konstant können zu einer Temperatur-Drosselung führen (140 W konstant gehen)." Test duration is not stated. The article gives no model number, only Amazon.de ASIN B0FG6ZTWPH; the 3-port, 160 W, 65 × 52 mm description matches the A2687, but match the ASIN to the model before use. Read-out: 28 V/5 A, PPS up to 4.5–21 V 5 A, AVS 15–28 V up to 140 W. No °C figures.

findings.label: 140 W at room temperature and weight (smartzone.de, Holger Becker, 2026-03-10)
findings.value: 140 W possible without problems at 20 °C room temperature; at 160 W across two loads it throttled after about 40 minutes to 100 W + 50 W; 218 g
findings.note: Quotes: "140W hingegen sind bei 20°C Zimmertemperatur problemlos möglich." and "Nach gut 40 Minuten drosselte das Gerät die Leistung auf jeweils 100W beziehungsweise 50W." Load was an Anker Solix C300 DC. How long the 140 W run lasted is not stated. Model A2687 named. Three weights now exist: 218 g (smartzone), 205 g (techtest.org), 220 g (our record).

findings.value: 131.8 W into a MacBook Pro 16; charger display read 136 W with one high-power device on USB-C1; USB-C1 offers 28 V/5 A, PPS 4–21 V 5 A, AVS 9–20 V; 337.5 g; 75.80 × 75.74 mm

The article's intro says 353 g and its weighing says 337.5 g; Notebookcheck says about 360 g. Efficiency and temperature are not measured there. AVS on C1 matters for the iPhone 18 Pro rule in the cluster map.

findings.label: What a 16-inch MacBook Pro actually draws (Notebookcheck, Andreas Osthoff, 2026-03-14)
findings.value: MacBook Pro 16 (M5 Pro) on the 140 W adapter: 145 W at peak, settling at 134 W; up to 147 W on a more powerful supply
findings.source_title: Apple tries to hide that the power adaptors of MacBook Pro models are insufficient
findings.note: Quote: "we measured a maximum consumption of 145 Watts, which eventually dropped to 134 Watts." This is why a charger that settles at 118–120 W matters for sustained heavy work, not only for the first 30 minutes of a fast charge. The article says the battery covers the small shortfall; it gives no discharge rate for the 16-inch model.

Macworld prints no measured output, temperature or efficiency for any charger; its only test statement is "All the chargers listed here have been tested and are trusted by Macworld." I read the first 100,000 of the page's 131,042 characters.

unsourced: Tom's Hardware's 20-charger test in its own words: the article body would not load in three attempts (only navigation came back), so the 118 W / 67.2 °C (Anker A2697) and 88 W / 76.4 °C (Baseus FH11) figures rest on verdictbits' report of them.

A sustained single-port 140 W run (30 minutes or longer) for the UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W X774: looked in Notebookcheck's review, ChargerLAB's teardown and search results for TechRadar and nextpit; none publishes one.
Case temperature in °C at 140 W for the UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W X774 and the Anker Prime 160W: Notebookcheck, ChargerLAB, techtest.org and smartzone.de give none.
Conversion efficiency for the UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W X774: ChargerLAB's teardown and Notebookcheck's review give none.
A measured time to 50% on a 16-inch MacBook Pro with any third-party 140 W charger: ChargerLAB's M4 Pro compatibility test has spot wattages only; I did not open its MacBook Pro M5 test.
A test of the AOHi Youth 140W US-plug unit sold today: the only bench test found is Chongdiantou's 2024 test of the China-market version.
Any named measurement for the UGREEN Nexode 200W, Plugable PS-EPR-140C1 or Insignia 140W: not searched within the call budget.
Prices: none re-read today; this angle covered measurements only, and the AOHi code was not retested.
